title: Strict positive definiteness of continuous isotropic positive kernels on a circle times a sphere of dimension at least two via all even and odd degree tails
author: Jean C. Guella; Valdir A. Menegatto; Ana P. Peron
source_title: Strictly Positive Definite Kernels on a Product of Spheres II
difficulty_reason: The proof handles arbitrary paired antipodal configurations and extracts independent even and odd spectral obstructions. Its sufficiency argument normalizes by the largest circle quadratic form, controls every mixed form by Cauchy-Schwarz and sends the off-diagonal Gegenbauer terms to zero along an unbounded degree subsequence. This joint tail criterion is stronger than testing positivity separately on the two factors.

proof_review.note: Complete3.11 characterization and all new3.1-3.10 support read: collapse against a circle interpolation vector, enlargement to antipodal enhanced sets, exact even/odd block decomposition, equivalence of the paired systems, and3.9 maximum-quadratic-form subsequence argument with normalized Gegenbauer decay. The continuous tail functions3.10 and prior circle arithmetic-progression strictness criterion then give3.11. The opposite parity case explicitly follows the identical displayed block proof with c1-c2 versus c1+c2; this is a bounded routine case, not a missing independent core. Both the native TeX line 409 and the visually inspected official PDF page 12 contain absolute-value bars in the normalized mixed-form Cauchy–Schwarz bound. The earlier text-extraction warning about a missing absolute value is unsupported and is removed. Original statement/proof bytes are preserved. Degree cutoff gamma is taken in N0 in the integer support sets. No higher two-point-homogeneous-space extension or sufficient-condition neighbor counted.

statement_scope: m>=2; real continuous isotropic positive-definite kernel on S1 times Sm with nonnegative summable double Chebyshev/Gegenbauer coefficients a_(k,l), and J_f^k={l:a_(k,l)>0}. Full3.11: strict positive definiteness iff for every integer gamma>=0 both integer sets {k in Z:some odd l>=gamma belongs to J_f^abs(k)} and {k in Z:some even l>=gamma belongs to J_f^abs(k)} intersect every full arithmetic progression j+dZ,d>=1. Both tail conditions are necessary. No m=1 or non-positive starting kernel case.
editorial_warning: Gamma is an integer degree cutoff in Theorem 3.11. Both the native TeX and visually inspected official PDF preserve the absolute-value bars in the Cauchy–Schwarz display; an earlier text-only extraction warning is removed.
